verses.1: Rehoboam went to Jerusalem. He gathered the people of Judah together. There were about a hundred thousand men who were ready to fight against Israel, in order to take back the queen’s throne for Rehoboam.
verses.2: And the word of Jehovah was spoken to Shemaiah, the man of God, as follows:
verses.3: Say to Rehobam, son of Solomon, king of Judah, and to all the Israelites in Judah and Nenin:
verses.4: So said Yahweh: “Do not go back to your homes, and do not fight against your brothers again. For from me will come this thing. And they will hear the words of Yahweh, and they will return from their rebellion against Jerusalem.”
verses.5: And Rehobam settled in Jerusalem, and he built cities for the people of Judah.
verses.6: And he built the house of bread, and the altar, and the tabernacle.
verses.7: And the house of Zor, and their fields, and their flocks.
verses.8: And Gath, and Merisha, and Ziph.
verses.9: And Adonai, and Lakish, and Azekah.
verses.10: And the Zerahites, and the Aylohites, and the Hebronites, who lived in Judah and in Benjamin, the cities of Mizraim.
verses.11: And he strengthened the forts, and gave them rulers and officials to manage them. He also provided them with food, wine, and oil.
verses.12: And in every city, they built fortresses and strongholds. They strengthened them greatly. Thus, Judea became a powerful kingdom during that time.
verses.13: And the priests and Levites, who were throughout all Israel, stood on him from every corner of the land.
verses.14: For the Levites abandoned their cities and their possessions, and went to Judah and Jerusalem. They were left behind by their ancestors and their sons, who became officials under Jehovah’s service.
verses.15: And he stood there, with shepherds and lambs, as well as calves, whom he created.
verses.16: And after them, all the tribes of Israel who dedicated their hearts to seeking Jehovah, the God of Israel. They came to Jerusalem to worship Jehovah, the God of their ancestors.
verses.17: And they strengthened the kingdom of Judah. They also supported Solomon’s son, Rehoboam, for six years, as they followed in the footsteps of David and Solomon.
verses.18: And Rehuel took a woman who had the same disease as the daughter of Jerimoth, son of David. Her father was Eliezer, son of Ishbak.
verses.19: And he had sons: Eshu, Shamarya, and Zaham.
verses.20: And after that, she took a wife from the family of Abishalom. She gave birth to Abiya, Aty, Zizya, and Shlomit.
verses.21: Rehuel loved Maachah, the daughter of Abishalom, more than any of his other wives. There were twenty women in her harem, and fifty concubines. She gave birth to forty sons and fifty daughters.
verses.22: And Rehuel stood at the head of the tribe of Reuben, with Abiyahu as his leader. He was chosen to rule over his brothers.
verses.23: And he created from all his descendants people for all the lands of Judah. He also created them for all the cities of the nations. He gave them many gifts. And he asked those women to become his wives.
